name: Bhapa Jadoh
ingredients: Aromatic rice (like joha or jasmine) - 1½ cups, washed and soaked 30 mins
Smoked pork (or chicken) - 250g, cut into bite-sized pieces
Fermented bamboo shoots (tung-rim) - ½ cup, rinsed and drained
Bamboo shoot tips (optional, fresh) - ¼ cup, sliced
Cilantro - ¼ cup, chopped for garnish
Banana leaves - for lining steamer (or parchment paper)
instructions: 1. In a mixing bowl, combine smoked pork pieces with turmeric powder, salt, grated ginger, and minced garlic. Let marinate for 15 minutes.

2. In a heavy-bottomed pan, heat mustard oil on medium-high. Sauté the marinated pork until browned, about 5 minutes. Add green chillies and fermented bamboo shoots; cook for 2 minutes until aromatic.

3. Drain the soaked rice and add it to the pan with the pork mixture. Stir gently to coat rice with oil and spices. Add 2½ cups of water and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 10 minutes until rice is half-cooked and water is absorbed.

4. Prepare a steamer. Line the steamer basket with banana leaves (or parchment). Transfer the half-cooked rice mixture into the lined basket, spreading evenly. If using fresh bamboo shoot tips, scatter over the top.
5. Steam over high heat for 25-30 minutes, until rice is tender and flavors are infused. Check water level occasionally; add boiling water if needed.
6. Remove from steamer, let rest 5 minutes. Gently fluff with a fork. Garnish with fresh cilantro. Serve hot, with a side of pickled vegetables or chutney.
description: A fragrant, soul-warming symphony of fermented bamboo and aromatic herbs, wrapped in the earthy embrace of fragrant rice.
